youtube_title: Halloween before trick-or-treat: what Indiana's old newspapers reported (1906-1917)
youtube:
Before trick-or-treat, Halloween in northwest Indiana was a night of pranks, and the papers kept score. 🎃 In 1906, Whiting put about 10 extra policemen on watch. Gates still vanished, and a window was broken at Recht's department store. In 1909, the paper said Halloween had gone "more quietly than it ever has been," then listed the damage: door mats and gates stolen "by the wholesale," and soap on the streetcar rails, so the motorman had to climb down and throw sand on them. By the 1920s, some towns tried to tame the night with parties and parades; Anoka, Minnesota, started its Halloween parade in 1920. And trick-or-treat? Its earliest known printing, from 1917 in Ontario, meant just what it said: a treat, or a trick. What did Halloween look like where you grew up? Tell us in the comments! #Halloween #HalloweenHistory #Indiana #LaPorte #Whiting #History #Shorts

All pictures are drawn. Narration is a computer voice. Sources: the 1906 and 1909 Whiting reports as quoted by the Whiting-Robertsdale Historical Society, "Halloween Has Always Brought Out the Wickedly in Whiting" (2018); Mental Floss and the Star Tribune on Anoka's 1920 parade; the Wisconsin Historical Society on 1920s parties and parades; SooToday, Barry Popik and the Dictionary of Canadianisms on the Sault Daily Star (Nov. 1, 1917). More LaPorte County history: https://laporteweathernow.com/history
